about: Table 1 of arXiv 1909.00175 v1 (Zou and Lu, 2019, “Joint Detection and Location of English Puns”), page 4: 15 rows by 13 columns, three header rows with spanning cells (Homographic and Heterographic over six columns each, Detection and Location over three). The image is this page's crop of the PDF page; the ground truth is the tabular in the paper's pun.tex (lines 244 to 277 of the arXiv source, kept in src/inputs/).
question_html:
The QASPER question this table answers
“What state-of-the-art results are achieved?” Annotated answer: F1 92.19 on homographic pun detection, 80.19 on homographic pun location, 89.76 on heterographic pun detection. The only evidence is this table, so a pipeline that loses its structure can retrieve the numbers and still not know which is which. The three cells are outlined in purple.
note: Adjacency F1: pairs of horizontally or vertically adjacent non-empty cells where at least one is a number, compared as text with the ground truth (the relation idea of the ICDAR 2013 table competition, restricted to the body so that merging the three header rows into one, as Docling does, is not penalised). Header association: the share of the table's numbers found in the right row whose column header text contains all three ground-truth header words. A parser that emits no table (plain text) has no grid, so neither score applies; “cells whose text appears” still counts a number found anywhere. Measured on Apple M1 Pro (CPU), default settings, 2026-10-14. Script: src/scripts/table_score.py.
